claims.text: Applying a TiB2 coating to boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The TiB2 coating will form a stable protective interfacial layer.
The TiB2 interfacial layer will resist chemical attack by molten aluminum.
The TiB2 interfacial layer will prevent or minimize aluminum infiltration into the boride-based substrate.
TiB2 has high chemical stability in contact with molten aluminum.
TiB2 has low solubility in molten aluminum.
The chemical stability and low solubility of TiB2 allow it to act as a barrier against aluminum attack.
Preventing direct contact between molten aluminum and the substrate will reduce the rate of material degradation.
TiB2-coated components will have significantly lower mass loss than uncoated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
TiB2-coated components will have significantly less surface degradation than uncoated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
The proposed improvement is expected during continuous contact with molten aluminum at 660–750°C.
The corrosion-resistance improvement should persist while the TiB2 coating remains intact and adherent.
Mechanical damage to the TiB2 coating may reduce its corrosion-protection effectiveness.
Exposure above the stability range of TiB2 may reduce the coating's effectiveness.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on TiB2 coating quality and thickness.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on the composition of the boride-based substrate and molten aluminum alloy.
